title: Practice: Design a Notification System
summary: Email, SMS, push and in-app, step by step: templates, user preferences, channel adapters, priorities, retries with backoff, idempotency, rate limits and delivery tracking.

steps.title: Clarify the requirements
hints: Who calls the system, and with what? A raw message, or an event plus a template id?
Think about the user: what would annoy them (spam, 3 a.m. pings, duplicates) and what must never be lost (OTPs)?
checklist: Channels: email, SMS, push, in-app
Templates with parameters (and localisation, at least mentioned)
User preferences: per-channel and per-category opt-outs, quiet hours
Priorities: transactional (OTP) vs. marketing
Retries, no duplicates, delivery status tracking

steps.title: Identify entities
hints: Separate the *request* (what a caller asks for) from each *delivery* (one channel, one attempt history).
Which part talks to Twilio/SES/FCM, and how do you keep their APIs out of your core?
checklist: Notification request vs. per-channel Delivery with status
Template and TemplateStore/renderer
UserPreferences / PreferenceStore
ChannelSender interface with provider adapters
RetryPolicy and a queue/dispatcher

steps.title: Draw the class diagram
hints: The service is a facade. Senders are behind one interface, keyed by channel.
Where do the checks that can *skip* a delivery go: preferences, quiet hours, rate limits?
checklist: NotificationService facade → queue, workers
ChannelSender interface with Email/SMS/Push/InApp implementations
A filter chain for preferences / quiet hours / rate limit
Delivery status tracked and observable

steps.title: Walk through the send flow
hints: Should the caller wait for the SMS to be sent? What does the API return?
Order the checks: what should run before rendering a template, and what after?
checklist: Accept → validate → dedupe → enqueue, returning an id quickly (async)
Worker: preferences/filters → render → send through the channel adapter
Retry on transient errors only; record status per channel
Priority queues so OTPs aren't stuck behind marketing

steps.title: Patterns: channels, filters, templates
hints: Adding WhatsApp should be a new class plus registration. What makes that true?
Preferences, quiet hours, rate limits and dedupe are a sequence of yes/no checks, which suggests one well-known pattern.
checklist: Strategy/Adapter: ChannelSender per channel/provider, registered in a map
Chain of Responsibility for delivery filters
Decorator for retry / failover / metrics around a sender
Observer for delivery status events; Builder for complex requests

steps.title: Reliability and concurrency
hints: The order service retries its API call after a timeout. The first call actually succeeded. What happens to the customer?
Two workers pick up the same message (at-least-once queue). Then what?
checklist: Idempotency key with an atomic check-and-mark
Exponential backoff with jitter; retryable vs. permanent errors
Dead-letter queue after max attempts
Per-user and per-provider rate limiting
Delivery state machine (PENDING → SENT → DELIVERED / FAILED)

steps.title: Code the core
hints: Write `ChannelSender`, `TemplateStore.render` and the preference check first, then the retry loop.
Inject the sleep function so the retry logic is testable without waiting.
checklist: Senders registered by channel (no switch on channel type)
Preference and opt-out checks before rendering
Retry with exponential backoff, only for retryable errors
Atomic idempotency check; per-channel results

steps.title: Answer the follow-ups
hints: Several of these are a new filter, a new sender decorator or a new queue. Say which.
Don't forget the user's experience: digests, timezones, unsubscribe links.
checklist: Scheduled notifications
Provider failover
Digests / batching
Adding a new channel (WhatsApp)
